children: , the diabetes-and-obesity pharmaceutical leader, brought Anthropic's Claude into its drug-research workflow, Reuters reported Wednesday. The U.S. depositary shares traded at $42.125. Novo will begin by testing Claude Science on selected scientific questions while also deploying Anthropic models for software-development work.

The partnership is about speed, not AI headlines. Novo and Anthropic want the models to sharpen biological reasoning and compress the time researchers spend moving from an idea to an actionable scientific decision. But there is still plenty investors do not know: no contract value, exclusivity terms, development milestones or quantified savings were disclosed. That makes execution the real story. Claude matters only if it helps Novo kill weak experiments earlier, move promising programs faster or strip friction out of a research machine spending billions to stay ahead in obesity and diabetes.

Novo produced DKK33.39 billion of adjusted operating profit from DKK78.49 billion of second-quarter sales, implying an adjusted operating margin of roughly 42.5%. The valuation picture is even more striking: the chart places the shares at $42.125 against a GF Value estimate of $105.13, leaving the market price 59.93% below that benchmark. That gap shows how much skepticism is already embedded in the stock. AI will not close it by itself; faster development decisions and stronger drug economics might.

title: Novo Drops as Claude Enters Drug Development
